o1.biggest_strength: Honest money with checkable working. It shows a range, applies 6% monthly churn after 90 days, and gives a blunt warning: the pause does 80% of the work, and without it the flow keeps fewer people than today. That sets a clear critical path for the sprint.
o1.biggest_mistake: The trip-over panel only lets people go. It gives no 'remind me before your next trip' or pause option for Greg-type learners. Also, the cancel button is inactive until a reason is picked, which comes close to the easy-cancel rule.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Add an optional 'email me before my next trip' line for goal or trip-over learners. Keep the cancel button live at all times. Add a holdout group to prove the new rates. Trim a little to sit comfortably under 1,000 words.

o2.biggest_strength: It covers more cases. There is a 'remind me in 3 or 6 months' option for trip-over, a smaller-goal option for learners who already set reminders, a cancel button that is always live, and a 10% holdout to test the assumptions. The build notes are concrete.
o2.biggest_mistake: It keeps the 50% off for app-switchers, the same offer that 61% abandon. It also values those 67 people at full price while labelling it 'after discount'. The yearly figure of £136k assumes no churn and gives no range.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Drop or justify the 50% off for switchers. Value discounted keeps at the discounted price. Apply realistic churn to the 12-month figure and give a low-to-high range. Flag that the whole gain depends on rebuilding the pause.

reason: Output 1 drops the half-price offer entirely, and its numbers are honest: a range, churn applied, and a clear warning that everything hangs on the pause. Output 2 has some nice touches, like the trip reminder and the holdout, but it keeps a discount we know fails and its revenue maths is rosier.
